text: {"question":"How does the H0 estimate obtained from the magnitude‑only Pantheon+ update compare to the H0 value derived when the full Pantheon+ dataset is used together with the Gaussian prior on the standardized SNIa absolute magnitude, and what is the combined effect of these two approaches on the inferred H0 value?","reference_answer":"The magnitude‑only Pantheon+ update yields H0 = 73.264 ± 0.806 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, while using the full Pantheon+ data with the MB = −19.253 ± 0.027 prior gives H0 ≈ 73.26 ± 0.98 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. Both approaches produce essentially the same H0 within uncertainties, indicating that the additional supernova information and the MB prior do not significantly shift the baseline H0 estimate."}
